uncertainty.method: Per-pixel change in dB (after minus before) after 9x9 multilook in linear power, minus the median change of all measurable pixels (+0.71 dB for HH). The no-change spread sigma (0.98 dB) is 1.4826 x the median absolute deviation of the change. A pixel counts as changed when its change is at least k x sigma and at least 2 dB, for k = 2, 3 and 4; patches that cannot hold a disk 11 pixels across are removed. Pixels within 1.5 dB of the estimated noise floor on both dates are excluded as 'cannot tell'.
notes: Each area is a range, not one value: low uses the strict threshold (4 sigma), central 3 sigma and high the lenient one (2 sigma). The sensitivity list shows how other processing choices move the central value.
HH: 13% of the area is at or below the noise floor on 2026-06-19, 16% on 2026-10-17 and 10% on both.
HV: 28% of the area is at or below the noise floor on 2026-06-19, 31% on 2026-10-17 and 25% on both.
The noise floor is estimated from the darkest part of each image, not from the instrument's noise record. Pixels at the floor on only one date are kept; their change is a lower bound.
Changed patches narrower than about 110 m are not counted, so thin features such as narrow channels or roads are under-represented.

caveats.text: 2026-06-19 and 2026-10-17 are provisional-tier (calibrated, but values may change after reprocessing).
Wind roughens open water and changes its brightness from one pass to the next. A change over water is not by itself a change of the surface.
On steep slopes the radar image is distorted (layover) or blind (shadow); changes there are unreliable.
A change in radar brightness means the surface scatters the signal differently (water level, moisture, roughness, vegetation, structures). It is not by itself a land-cover label.

params.sigma_estimator: 1.4826 x median absolute deviation of the change
params.speck_removal: binary opening with a disk 11 pixels across

# Needs: pip install -e backend/  and an Earthdata Login in ~/.netrc (or EARTHDATA_TOKEN).
# Reads the best calibration tier available when it runs. This result used:
#   NISAR_L2_PR_GCOV_023_077_A_027_4005_DHDH_A_20260619T124759_20260619T124835_P05023_N_F_J_001 (provisional)
#   NISAR_L2_PR_GCOV_033_077_A_027_4005_DHDH_A_20261017T124756_20261017T124831_P05023_N_F_J_001 (provisional)
from nisar_investigator.schemas import ChangeRequest
from nisar_investigator.workflows.change import run_change

if __name__ == "__main__":  # required: the reader starts worker processes
    result = run_change(ChangeRequest(
        bbox=(-120.56, 50.675, -120.4, 50.735), date_before="2026-06-19", date_after="2026-10-17", track=77, polarization="HH",
    ))
    print(result.summary.headline)
    for m in result.summary.metrics:
        print(m.key, m.low, m.central, m.high, m.unit)

report.answer: Between 19 June and 17 October 2026, 0.22–0.92 km² brightened (HH) and 0.16–1.01 km² darkened (HH) in the 84 km² area. The Thompson River gauge (8.4 km away) dropped from 5.44 m to 2.47 m.
observed: Radar brightness rose over 0.22–0.92 km² (HH) and 0.09–0.18 km² (HV), fell over 0.16–1.01 km² (HH) and 0.11–0.17 km² (HV) of the 84 km² area between 19 June and 17 October 2026. [chg_20261115_7fea3739]
The Thompson River at Kamloops dropped from 5.44 m on 19 June to 2.47 m on 17 October 2026. [ctx_river_gauges]
possible_explanations: Darkening may reflect lower water levels exposing drier lakebed; brightening could indicate vegetation regrowth or increased moisture. To check: Compare with soil moisture data or field surveys
unknown: Whether the river gauge's drop directly affected lake conditions
Specific land-cover changes driving the radar signal
report.confidence: medium: Radar changes are statistically significant but ambiguous; river gauge data provides context but measures a different location.
